label: copy-phase input g (g just echoed back), stronger when the next output is in a preferred token set
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only at steps where the fed-back input is g, meaning the model just output g. (phase==2)&(in_tok==g) has recall 1.0 and mass recall 1.0 on dev, but precision is only 0.24 (F1 0.39), so most copy-phase g inputs leave it silent. Whether it fires depends a lot on the token being output next (the original token after g): g, 2, 1, l, h, p fire about 5x more often, then m, k, i, t, s, 3. Restricting to those 12 next tokens gives dev P 0.48 / R 0.81 / F1 0.60 / mass recall 0.87. The leftover activations are weak and spread over other next tokens. Never fires in the original or delimiter phase, or on any other input token. Rates are highest at recall_idx 2-6 and low at recall_idx 1 and 8. Requiring that g was seen exactly once before does not help. The largest activations come from a single g in the middle of the sequence followed by 1/2/p, e.g. a l g 1 2 ...; a second g in a gg run activates less. Precision stays incomplete: activation is graded and the next-token lookup only partly separates firing from non-firing.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: g, -, e, 0, j, n; least: 1, v, s, <DEL>) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: g, 1, l, p; input phase: ; delimiter step: ); timing cues that raise it most: L=4 & t=7, L=4 & t=6, L=7 & t=8.
